subject: Mathematics
overall_notes: Strong G2 capstone. Lesson cleanly bridges D1.1-D1.5 with the personal-not-data trap (a real grade-2 misconception) and concrete recovery moves (sentence frames, group+mode drill, data-tells-me frame). Materials are everyday with explicit OPTIONAL puppet substitution. Detective Dot/Tally anchor minds_on, action, and consolidation; success criteria all start with 'I can'; exit routine is a memorable 'My mode was ___. So most children chose ___' frame. Mathematical authenticity is solid: mode defined precisely as 'most common', conclusions framed as group-level data summaries (not opinion), and the misconception is named in research-grounded terms (personal-not-data trap). Worksheet practises every named success criterion (tally -> bar graph + mode -> conclusion) with sentence-frame scaffolds. Lesson_worksheet_consistency lands at 3 rather than 4 because the worksheet is essentially a rote repeat of the action steps (Part 1 tally, Part 2 bar+mode, Part 3 conclusion) with the same survey size; a Level 4 transfer task would deliberately vary format (e.g., analyse a pre-built bar graph the child didn't survey) with explicit justification. Passes the strict bar (no <3, exactly one =3).
